name: Clear and restart the print spooler
summary: Stops the print spooler, removes every queued print job, and starts it again: the fix for a stuck print queue.
risk_note: Every job waiting to print on this endpoint is lost and has to be sent again. A spooler that has been disabled (often deliberately, as hardening against print-spooler vulnerabilities) is left disabled.

windows: Stops the Print Spooler service (and the services that depend on it).
Deletes the queued job files from the spool directory (%SystemRoot%\System32\spool\PRINTERS, or the one configured in the registry). Printers, drivers and their settings are untouched.
Starts the spooler and any dependent service that was running. Does nothing on an endpoint whose spooler is disabled or absent.
linux: Cancels every queued job on every CUPS printer (cancel -a) and restarts CUPS. Printers and their settings are untouched. Does nothing where CUPS is not installed.
darwin: Cancels every queued job on every printer (cancel -a) and restarts cupsd. Printers and their settings are untouched.
